findings.issue: ARGV_PROSE_FLAGS is a hand-typed copy of audit-task.py's PROSE_FLAGS (audit-task.py:1000) and already omits --rename, --no-evidence-reason, --issue, --resolution, --repro, --expected, --actual, --override-verdict (read, and confirmed by running the lint on scratch snippets: ["done", "--no-evidence-reason", built] and ["retarget", "--rename", built] both return []). A reintroduced argv call on any of those flags, each one the verb gap-checks, passes the lint, so 'no call site can regress' holds for 8 of the 16 flags the verb checks. The comment justifies only --review-outcome.
findings.resolution: Derive the set from the verb: load audit-task.py by basename (_loader) and take its PROSE_FLAGS (dest -> --flag), minus one declared exemption {review_outcome} with its reason. Then a flag added to PROSE_FLAGS is linted by default.

findings.issue: The lint reads only 'literal flag, then non-Constant neighbour in one List/Tuple/Call'. Probed on scratch snippets, it returns [] for: a.append("--text"); a.append(built) (two calls); ["note", "--text=" + built] and "--text=%s" % built (joined form); FLAG = "--text"; [FLAG, built] (flag held in a name). It also fires on a legitimate value held in a named constant (["--reason", NOTE_CONST]) and on a literal concatenation ("a" + "b"), because any non-Constant counts as built. mt3 only pins the list, tuple and += shapes.
findings.resolution: Resolve module-level string constants before comparing; treat a BinOp/JoinedStr/Mod whose left literal starts with a prose flag plus '=' as a hit; add consecutive-append detection (an Expr call to .append with a prose-flag literal followed by a non-literal append on the same receiver); count a Name that resolves to a module constant string, and a BinOp of two literals, as literal. Add an mt3/mt4 row for each.

findings.issue: The helper exemption is blanket: spared.update(id(arg) for arg in node.args) also spares any Call passed as an argument of _verb_with_text, so _verb_with_text(c, s, _task_args(c, "note", t, "--text", built), "--reason", x) reports nothing (probed: []). The sparing exists only so the helper's own flag/text neighbours are not read, but that is already achieved by spare-ing the helper Call node itself.
findings.resolution: Spare only the helper call node's own positional list; do not add its argument Call nodes to `spared`, so nested argv builders are still read.

findings.issue: The helper docstring says a blank text on argv has 'nothing in it for a check to read'. A whitespace-only text such as '  ' is truthy to the verb and matches `\A[ \t]+` (audit-task.py:875) so it is refused on argv, exactly as '-' with whitespace-only stdin is refused (audit-task.py:1076). Also the stdin route rstrip('\n')s (audit-task.py:1075), so built text ending in newlines is not verbatim, which the docstring's 'arrives verbatim' omits. No regression (argv behaved the same before) but the stated reason is wrong.
findings.resolution: Reword to say blank means empty after strip and goes as-is because the verb treats an empty value as legal and a whitespace-only one is refused on either route, and note the trailing-newline strip; or normalise whitespace-only to '' before sending.

preExisting.issue: widen_task is scope then note, two verb calls with no rollback. If the scope call succeeds and the note call stops, the task's files already contain the new path, so a re-run computes new == [] (line 1417) and returns None without ever writing the note: a half-done widen that is never completed. The old loop had the same order and the same hole; splitting it into two statements does not change it, and routing the note through stdin removes the F743 way for the note to fail.
preExisting.resolution: Write the note first (it is idempotent to repeat) or compute `new` from the note's presence as well as the files, so a retry finishes the pair.

intent.note: Clause 'every such call passes the value as `-` and the text on stdin, through one helper in the drive': the six built-string prose values in drive-phase.py (widen note --text :1425, bug-add --description :1608, done --intent-basis :1740, block --reason :2991, done --no-change --reason :3066, signoff --summary :4146) all go through _verb_with_text; a grep of scripts/hooks for the prose flags finds no other call except full-gate.py:399, owned by P130.49. The strings are built by the same expressions as before, so only the transport changed: nothing lost or doubled, apart from stdin dropping trailing newlines (finding 4). widen_task keeps the scope-then-note order of the old loop; scope succeeding and note failing leaves the same half-done state as before (preExisting 1). Clause 'a lint case ... fails when a `_verb_or_stop` call carries a non-literal value after --text/--reason/--description': implemented as argv_prose_violations, a neighbour scan over List/Tuple/Call positionals; it covers the shipped shapes but is a hand-copied flag list and misses several realistic forms (findings 1-3). The three values left on argv: --review-outcome carries 'phase review filed at head' + 12 chars of a git head, no gap shape, and stdin carries one flag per call (signoff already spends it on --summary), safe. --accept-open ID=summary (drive-phase.py:4141) is not in PROSE_FLAGS and the verb only partition('=')s and strips it (audit-task.py:10902), so a doubled space in the summary is accepted today; safe, but it would break if the verb ever adds it to PROSE_FLAGS, and nothing links the two. bug-add title positional is gap-checked (PROSE_POSITIONAL) but is a fixed template over branch, 7-char sha and run id, so it holds no run of spaces while those are non-empty; safe. The executor's claim describes the diff accurately.
intent.redFirstBasis: The executor's basis names the command `test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage mt-block` in a throwaway tree at HEAD, exit 1, collected tests mt1, mt2 and mt3 failing assertions (the task's own cases), passing with the working tree's implementation; mt4 is the allow-direction case. That is a command, a non-zero exit, collected tests and the task's own cases failing an assertion. The stamp reads stale (moved head) by the brief's account, not weighed.
intent.inheritedTestsBasis: tests.gate's `selftests` entry is `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py`, which runs the whole project's selftests, and `validate`, `gate`, `report`, `lint`, `shots` and `interactive` are likewise project-wide, so no bounded selection of tests exists to ask the question of.
